findings.title: Global canManage() grants manage access with only the VIEW scope
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg) falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Including VIEW in a manage check means an admin holding only a `view` scope permission on the all-groups resource is considered able to manage groups. This method is used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` (`auth.groups().requireManage()`) and by `canManage(GroupModel)` callers, so a view-only admin could create, update, or delete top-level groups — a privilege escalation compared to canManage(GroupModel), which correctly checks only MANAGE. The expectedScopes for the global manage check should be MANAGE only.

findings.title: NPE when per-group resource and all-groups resource are both absent
findings.body: In hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes), when `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` returns null, the code calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, which returns null whenever the resource type resource does not exist or the schema is not supported for the resource server. The result is passed straight to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later `resource.getScopes()` without a null check, causing a NullPointerException (500 error) instead of a clean `false` for admins without any group permissions. The analogous UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission has the same shape; at minimum the new GroupPermissionsV2 copy needs a null guard.

findings.title: Removal of cached canViewGlobal causes repeated permission evaluation per subgroup
findings.body: getSubGroups previously computed `canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView()` once and short-circuited the filter. Now `auth.groups()::canView` is evaluated per subgroup. For an admin without the manage-users/view-users roles, each invocation of the V1 (and V2) global canView() runs a full authorization-policy evaluation against the admin permissions resource server, so listing a group with many subgroups performs N policy evaluations instead of one. The same pattern was removed in GroupsResource.getGroups. Cache the global result (or make canView() memoize) to avoid the per-element evaluation cost.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong method
findings.body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says "Throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false" — copy-pasted from requireManageMembership. It should reference canManageMembers(GroupModel). Since this PR adds javadoc to the whole interface, the newly written contract text is wrong for this method and will mislead implementers/users of the evaluator.

findings.title: resolveGroup only accepts the internal group id, unlike users/clients which also accept names
findings.body: resolveUser and resolveClient fall back to lookup by username/clientId when the id lookup fails, but resolveGroup only does getGroupById. When creating a group policy via getOrCreateResource with a group name or path instead of the internal id, the method throws IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object..."). Either this asymmetry is intentional (then it deserves a comment) or the group path/name lookup is missing; as written, the API behaves inconsistently across resource types and callers passing a group path get a 500-level error.

findings.title: getScope NPEs when resourceType is null or unknown
findings.body: In getScope, when the schema is supported, `SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType)` is dereferenced without a null check. If a caller passes a null or unrecognized resourceType (e.g., a permission being created without a resource type before validation runs), this throws a NullPointerException instead of the intended ModelValidationException ("Scope %s was not found for resource type %s."). A null/unknown-type check with a meaningful validation error is needed.
